slice: A17 — runtime config, branding/legal documents and feature capability truth

prs.dependency_order: core and user are independent (no OpenAPI change in either, so no contract-ci ordering); meta lands last
prs.migration: none — core stays at schema 132, search at 18

lab.topology: one origin — a pipe-only node proxy on 127.0.0.1:3100 in front of `node .next/standalone/server.js` on :3000 and vidra-core on :8088 — because vidra_refresh is SameSite=Lax, Path=/api/v1/auth
processes_observed_separately: vidra-core VIDRA_ROLE=worker — a real second process, no HTTP listener (curl to its HTTP_PORT returns nothing, and it logs 'worker-only process ready; no HTTP listener in this role')
Next.js production standalone server, separate process
lab.postgres: native PostgreSQL 16.15 on a private port (55432), fresh cluster, database vidralab at core schema 132 / search ledger 18
lab.redis: native redis on a private port (56379); core on db 0, search on db 1
lab.frontend: production `next build` served from .next/standalone with .next/static and public copied in; NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL baked to the proxy origin, INTERNAL_API_BASE_URL to core's real port
lab.browser: real Chromium against that origin, hard reload between states
lab.rate_limits: shipped defaults, never raised — 380 core requests across the slice, ZERO 429s; 391 search requests, all 200
lab.actors: mona (owner/admin via the one-time setup token), cleo (ordinary user; briefly promoted to moderator for the role spot-check and demoted back), anonymous
lab.teardown: core api + worker, vidra-search, the Next server, the proxy, redis and postgres all stopped; the data directory and lab directory removed. No lab artefact is committed.

sc1_registry_truth.cross_check: the static registry parse of internal/instancesettings/service.go `specs` and the live GET /admin/instance-settings both report 116

default_source.note: only 20 of 116 keys take their default from parsed config, so for the other 96 NO env var and NO compose ${VAR:-…} fallback can move anything — the registry's hardcoded default is the only fallback

sc1_registry_truth.precedence_rule: DB overlay row (instance_settings) > the process's env var > the Go default — some of which are DERIVED from other env — with compose ${VAR:-…} fallbacks materialising as ordinary env, so at runtime a compose fallback is indistinguishable from an operator's own export.

three_layer_proof_on_live_enabled.L1_go_derived_default: no env, no DB row: GET /admin/instance-settings reports default=false value=false, and GET /instance features.live=false — the Go default is `p.Bool("FEATURE_LIVE_ENABLED", liveRTMPURL != "")`
three_layer_proof_on_live_enabled.L3_db_beats_L1: PATCH {"live_enabled": true} -> value=true overridden=true, public features.live=true
three_layer_proof_on_live_enabled.L2_env_moves_the_default: restart with FEATURE_LIVE_ENABLED=true -> default flips to true
three_layer_proof_on_live_enabled.L3_beats_L2: same process, DB row live_enabled=false -> value=false overridden=true default=true; public features.live=false
three_layer_proof_on_live_enabled.reset: PATCH {"live_enabled": null} deletes the row (0 rows in instance_settings) and the env default returns

runtime_refresh_tiers.writing_api_process: immediate — Apply() persists then reloads its own cache synchronously
runtime_refresh_tiers.every_other_core_process_incl_workers: <= 10s — settingsversion.DefaultInterval, one counter row polled by EVERY role (measured: worker reload 9s after the PATCH)
runtime_refresh_tiers.frontend_ssr: <= 60s — lib/instance-config.server.ts INSTANCE_CONFIG_REVALIDATE_SECONDS, matching the backend's Cache-Control: s-maxage=60 on GET /instance
runtime_refresh_tiers.vidra_search: push, not poll — a change to any of the 7 SearchSettingKeys posts search.config_updated to POST /internal/v1/events (HMAC) at once

sc1_registry_truth.boot_baked_layer: NONE of the 116 overlay keys is boot-baked: every consumption site reads through a provider closure (verified by reading every `instancesettings.Key*` reference in cmd/api and internal/httpapi). What IS boot-only is the ENV side beside them — STORAGE_BACKEND, the KEKs, JWT_SECRET, LIVE_RTMP_URL/LIVE_HLS_ROOT, WHISPER_ENDPOINT, FEDERATION_ENABLED, IPFS_*, DELIVERY_CDN_BASE_URL, MAIL/SMTP, YTDLP_IMPORT_ENABLED — which is ANDed in at the seam. Effective = setting AND boot capability.
sc1_registry_truth.frontend_origin_precedence: runtime-injected /runtime-config.js (PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL on the running container) > build-inlined NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL > "" same-origin in production / http://localhost:8080 in dev — documented in lib/config.ts and mirrored by the force-dynamic runtime-config route

branding_string.rss: GET /feeds/videos.xml <title>A17 Lab Tube</title> and 'Latest public videos on A17 Lab Tube' — immediate
branding_string.frontend_title_and_og: <title>A17 Lab Tube</title>, og:title, og:site_name, twitter:title all follow within the 60s SSR window (measured: picked up on the first poll)

runtime_int_limit.boundary: POST /admin/instance-settings/validate refuses 10 with 'must be 0 or an integer between 60 and 2592000'; upload_max_size_bytes -5 refused with its own range; search_mode 'nonsense' refused with the option list
runtime_int_limit.all_or_nothing: PATCH {instance_description: <valid>, search_mode: 'nonsense'} -> 422 and instance_description was NOT written (0 rows)

worker_read_setting.setting: live_max_duration_secs — read by the live duration watchdog, which runs ONLY in worker roles (30s ticker)
worker_read_setting.method: a live_streams row flipped to state='live' with started_at 2 hours ago; the PATCH was issued against the API process only
worker_read_setting.result: the worker process (started 23:35:26, never restarted) logged the poller reload at 23:42:04 — 9s after the 23:41:55 PATCH — and force-closed the session at 23:42:26 with max_duration_secs=60 and next_state=ended. The api process logged no watchdog line at all.
worker_read_setting.conclusion: the role-gated-poller defect prior audits flagged is ALREADY FIXED (core#115) and is now proven end-to-end against a real worker process: settingsversion.Poller runs in every role and is deliberately not leader-gated

worker_defect_found_and_fixed.what: the settings reach the worker, but two worker LOOPS were started on a once-at-boot reading of a runtime-dynamic predicate
worker_defect_found_and_fixed.repro_on_origin_main: YTDLP_IMPORT_ENABLED=true, channel_sync_enabled at its default (off) at boot. PATCH channel_sync_enabled=true -> GET /instance features.channel_sync=true; POST /channel-syncs -> 201 state=waiting_first_run; the worker's poller logged the reload; `grep -c 'channel auto-sync worker started'` on the worker = 0. The row moved only after the worker was restarted.
worker_defect_found_and_fixed.second_instance: the same shape gates the auto-caption (Whisper) drain loop on transcription_enabled
worker_defect_found_and_fixed.fix: core#179 — both services expose BootCapable() (the deployment prerequisite alone) and cmd/api gates the two worker starts on it; Enabled() is unchanged and still gates every request and every tick, so a loop started while the toggle is off is an immediate no-op
worker_defect_found_and_fixed.proof_of_fix: fixed binary, worker booted at 23:59:18 with the toggle OFF -> drain loop started anyway (1 line) and logged no sync work; admin turned the toggle on and created a sync -> the SAME process (still 23:59:18) claimed it, waiting_first_run -> syncing, no restart

search_relevant_setting.pushed: PATCH {search_mode: advanced, search_min_query_user_count: 7} -> POST /internal/v1/events on vidra-search answered 200 within the same second
search_relevant_setting.persisted: search.service_config rewritten atomically (one updated_at for all 8 rows): search_mode=advanced, minimum_query_user_count=7, plus the derived hide_sensitive_default
search_relevant_setting.not_pushed_by_design: search_service_enabled is core-side routing policy and is deliberately absent from SearchSettingKeys
search_relevant_setting.unverified: vidra-search's SERVING behaviour under the new config was not exercised — the lab index was empty (no videos published), so GET /search/suggestions returned an empty list both with the flag on and with it off. Delivery and persistence are proven; ranking/suggestion behaviour is not.

restart_round.runtime_values_persist: after restarting core api, core worker and vidra-search: instance_name, live_enabled, live_max_duration_secs and transcription_enabled all survived (they live in instance_settings, not in env); search.service_config survived vidra-search's own restart
restart_round.boot_baked_takes_effect_only_on_restart: adding LIVE_RTMP_URL + LIVE_HLS_ROOT moved the /admin/infrastructure live row from configured=false to configured=true and populated the live block — a change no runtime toggle can make

documents.names: homepage | custom_css | custom_js (a CHECK constraint on instance_documents, migration 0085); an unknown name is 404
documents.caps: homepage 100KiB, custom_css/custom_js 200KiB each — a 200KiB+1 body is refused 422 'must be at most 204800 bytes'
documents.round_trip: PUT homepage -> the public route returns the body verbatim with its sha256; /instance reports homepage.enabled=true and the hash for cache busting
documents.sanitisation: NONE server-side, deliberately — a <script> tag inside the homepage markdown is stored and returned byte-for-byte. The document store is raw; safety lives at the render seam (the homepage is markdown rendered by the frontend) and in the admin-only write gate. Stated, not changed.
documents.delivery_headers: custom.css text/css; custom.js application/javascript; both Cache-Control: public, max-age=300, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, and consumed hash-busted (?v={hash})

images.slots: avatar, banner, and four typed logo slots (favicon, header-wide, header-square, opengraph)
images.upload: multipart field "file"; POST returns 201 and GET /instance branding flips is_fallback false with a URL
images.og_and_favicon: after uploading the opengraph and favicon slots the public home page serves og:image and twitter:image pointing at /api/v1/instance/logo/opengraph, and <link rel="icon"> switches from the built-in /icon.svg to /api/v1/instance/logo/favicon (within the 60s SSR window)
images.validation: a text/plain body is refused 415 'unsupported media type'
images.delete: DELETE returns 204 and restores the fallback (is_fallback true, public route back to 404); a second DELETE on an unset slot is 404

sc3_documents_and_images.wrong_actors: anonymous 401 and ordinary user 403 on GET/PATCH /admin/instance-settings, POST /admin/instance-settings/validate, PUT /admin/instance-documents/{name}, POST /admin/instance-avatar and GET /admin/infrastructure|system; a MODERATOR is 403 on every one of them (these are admin-only, not staff routes). sc4_capability_truth.verdict: PASS after the fix in user#176; one product ruling recorded

live_with_no_ingest.observed: FEATURE_LIVE_ENABLED=true (which is exactly what the compose fallback injects) with no LIVE_RTMP_URL/LIVE_HLS_ROOT: GET /instance features.live=true; POST /channels/{handle}/live answers 201 with a stream key and NO rtmp_url field. transcription_with_no_whisper.observed: features.transcription=false because it ANDs the boot capability, so the frontend hides the affordance correctly — but the admin toggle itself said nothing about WHISPER_ENDPOINT beyond static help prose
transcription_with_no_whisper.fixed: user#176 declares a `warn` on transcription_enabled keyed on the infra snapshot's captions.configured. Verified in Chromium.

sc4_capability_truth.mail_dependent_flows: features.mail=false with no SMTP; the three mail keys (email_subject_prefix, email_body_signature, registration_require_email_verification) already carry a bootDep note that DISABLES the row with an explanation — rendered and verified in Chromium as the positive control for the mechanism
sc4_capability_truth.delivery_presign_and_cdn: both already carry a `warn` (never bootDep, so an on-but-inert switch stays flippable) — rendered and verified in Chromium as the second positive control
sc4_capability_truth.infrastructure_page_coverage: 15 capability rows with enabled/configured/note: object_storage, mail, search, federation, atproto, atproto_login, malware_scan, captions, live, ipfs, cdn, drm, tracing, metrics, vp9_alternates
sc4_capability_truth.infrastructure_reads_boot_config_by_desi: admin_infra.go's header states the rule explicitly and names live as the motivating case: the page must be able to CONTRADICT a toggle that says on. Two rows break it on purpose (cdn's enabled half, object_storage's note). Consequence, verified: with live_enabled turned OFF at runtime the infra live row still reports enabled=true. Recorded as designed, not filed as a defect.
sc4_capability_truth.build_baked_frontend_flags: CONFIRMED: still no live members. The only NEXT_PUBLIC_* value in the app is NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL, documented as the dev/e2e override and superseded at runtime by /runtime-config.js (a force-dynamic route). There are no build-baked feature flags at all.
sc4_capability_truth.four_mechanisms_summary: build-baked frontend flags (empty), compose ${VAR:-…} fallbacks, env, DB overlay. Of the 20 env-backed registry defaults, the core compose file pins a value for 11 of them and every one MATCHES the Go static default — except FEATURE_LIVE_ENABLED:-true, whose Go default is DERIVED (liveRTMPURL != ""). That single fallback is the whole shadowing problem.

sc5_custom_css_js.confirmation_path: client-side, in InstanceDocumentEditor with dangerConfirm: a modal headed 'This JavaScript runs in every visitor's browser' — 'Saving injects this script into every page, for every visitor — signed in or not. A mistake can break the site; malicious code can steal sessions. Only save code you wrote or fully trust.' — requiring the typed phrase 'run this code' (CUSTOM_JS_CONFIRM_PHRASE). Custom CSS has no typed confirmation; Clear on either has a second inline 'Clear it' confirm.
sc5_custom_css_js.unconfirmed_not_applied: typing 'yes do it' and pressing 'Save and run it' did nothing; the stored body was unchanged in the database
sc5_custom_css_js.confirmed_applied: typing 'run this code' saved; on a public page the new hash-busted <script src=.../instance/custom.js?v={hash}> loaded and ran (window.__A17_SECOND__ === true, data-a17b='ran2') while the previous script's marker was gone
sc5_custom_css_js.anonymous: proven with NO session at all before any login: custom CSS applied (body outline computed rgb(255,0,255) 3px) and custom JS executed on the public home page
sc5_custom_css_js.removed_gone: Clear -> 'Clear it': the script tag is absent from the page, the marker attribute is gone, and the row is deleted; the custom CSS left in place still applied, so the removal was scoped
sc5_custom_css_js.server_side: the confirmation is a CLIENT guard on an admin-only route — curl PUT /admin/instance-documents/custom_js succeeds with no confirmation. That is the honest shape: the route is requireRole(admin) and audited (admin.instance_document.update with name + content hash, never the body).
sc5_custom_css_js.csp: the frontend ships Content-Security-Policy-REPORT-ONLY (lib/security-headers.ts), script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' 'wasm-unsafe-eval'. Report-only enforces nothing today, and even enforced, custom.js is same-origin under the single-origin topology, so 'self' would allow it. The external-file delivery (rather than inlining) is what keeps a future enforced script-src 'self' viable — stated in the OpenAPI description.
sc5_custom_css_js.xss_surface_honestly: custom_js is arbitrary JavaScript on every page for every visitor including anonymous ones, same-origin, with full DOM and same-origin fetch access. Only an admin can set it (moderator 403, ordinary user 403, anonymous 401), every write is audited, and the confirmation modal says so in those words. Not widened into a CSP redesign.

unverified: vidra-search's serving behaviour under a changed search config — the lab index was empty, so suggestion/ranking output could not be distinguished from the empty-index case. Delivery of search.config_updated and its persistence in search.service_config ARE proven.
npm run e2e and the e2e-backed suite (need a browser fleet and a full backend) — repo CI covers them

the auto-caption worker half of the core fix was proven by unit test and by code symmetry, not by a live Whisper deployment (no transcription backend in the lab); the channel-sync half was proven end-to-end on two binaries
a real RTMP publisher — LIVE_RTMP_URL was set to prove the boot-baked flip only; INT-01 still owns actual ingest
findings_recorded_not_fixed: GET /instance features.live is the raw live_enabled setting, unlike every neighbouring row. PRODUCT RULING NEEDED: hide live when the ingest plane is absent (consistent with the struct literal) or keep showing it and rely on the admin-side explanation (consistent with admin_infra.go's documented 'contradict, do not hide' stance, now reinforced by the new settings-page warn).

The compose fallback FEATURE_LIVE_ENABLED: ${FEATURE_LIVE_ENABLED:-true} in vidra-core/docker-compose.yml shadows the Go DERIVED default (liveRTMPURL != ""), so the stock stack advertises live on an instance with no ingest plane. It is the only one of the 11 pinned fallbacks that disagrees with its Go default. Deliberately not changed here — it is a one-line compose edit with fleet-wide behaviour consequences and belongs to a decision, not a drive-by.

The auth screens are deliberately pinned to the product wordmark (AuthPage.tsx, asserted by apple-ux.spec), so a renamed instance still reads 'Sign in to Vidra' while the tab title correctly shows the instance name. PRODUCT QUESTION, not a defect.

Every statically prerendered route (all of /admin/*, /login) ships with the FALLBACK branding baked in, because a CI build has no backend to snapshot; the first ISR revalidation (~1 min) corrects it. Observed live: the header read 'Vidra' on a freshly built admin page and 'A17 Lab Tube' a minute later. Bounded and consistent with the documented 60s window.

The homepage document is stored and served without server-side sanitisation, including a <script> tag. Safe today because the frontend renders it as markdown, but the store itself offers no guarantee — worth a note if another renderer is ever added.

GET /admin/instance-settings reports key/type/value/default/overridden/page/section but NOT which processes read a key, nor its refresh tier. An operator cannot tell from the API that a change reaches a worker within 10s. Enhancement, not a defect.

for_adm04.admin_system: GET /admin/system reports 7 components — ffmpeg, postgres, redis, s3, search, settings_sync, smtp — plus rate_limits and a pgx pool block. settings_sync is the settings-version poller's health record and is api-only by design (a worker has no HTTP surface to report on), so a worker whose every poll fails is visible in logs and NOWHERE in the API. That is a real gap for ADM-04 to weigh.
for_adm04.no_secrets: admin_infra.go maintains an absolute never-list (no DSN, no S3 keys, no SMTP credentials, no JWT_SECRET, no *_KEK, no LIVE_INGEST_SECRET, no SEARCH_INTERNAL_SECRET, no IPFS cluster token) with a test asserting none appears in the body. Spot-checked in the lab: the response carried the local storage root and the RTMP URL, both non-secret by that list's own reasoning, and nothing else.
for_adm04.degraded_dependency_shape: the enabled/configured/note triple on /admin/infrastructure is the existing vocabulary for 'wired but off' vs 'on but unwired'; ADM-04's degraded-dependency work should reuse it rather than invent a second one.
for_adm04.lab_recipe: the two-process core topology in `lab` above is what ADM-04 needs to see a failed job on a worker while the api reports health — reuse it verbatim.
for_adm04.audit: every instance-settings write and every document write is audited; admin.instance_document.update records the document NAME and CONTENT HASH and never the body.

caught_by_ci: nothing in this slice was caught by CI — both defects needed a two-process lab with a real worker to see at all, and the missing dependency notices needed a real Chromium against a live backend.
